## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhotakamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Dhotaka") is the sixth discourse of the *Pārāyaṇavagga*, the fifth chapter of the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 5.6, PTS Snp 204, beginning at verse 1061) [Hazra 1994; Norman 1997–2001; Anderson & Smith 1913]. The text records a dialogue in which the student Dhotaka approaches the Buddha asking how one can attain freedom from all doubt. In response to Dhotaka's aspiration to hear his utterance and learn his own extinction (*nibbāna*), the Buddha explains that by being wise, mindful, and knowing the highest Dhamma, a practitioner overcomes doubt, attains tranquility and independence, and eliminates desire and craving for renewed existence [Hazra 1994; Anderson & Smith 1913].
